First-touch grading (skills seat, session `session_01WswfK2yNYT9hNnMH6TzAwL`): **into the decision inbox** (`needs-user-decision`) — the discriminating fact (what the Settings ruleset actually holds) is readable by the maintainer only (agents get HTTP 403, measured in the script header), so no seat can adjudicate this.

Four-prism block:

- **① Platform long-term coherence**: the required-context registry is trusted as contract; a row whose `authorized` line is screenshot-era invites the same collision class that cost #9495 a full pre-flight stop the same day. Reconciling keeps the registry's single-source-of-truth claim honest instead of accreting dated exceptions.
- **② Measured business pull**: real, same-day measurement — not speculative. Cost of the decision: one Settings look, one sentence. Cost of not deciding: every future retirement/rename card that touches `Build Docs` / `Console Pin Gate` risks another stop-and-report cycle.
- **③ AI-agent error-resistance**: agents structurally cannot verify Settings; the registry is the only machine-readable stand-in. A knowingly-stale row is the worst shape (reads as authoritative, is not); either a dropped row or a dated inert note is machine-honest.
- **④ Startup scope discipline**: no capability added either way — this is pure ledger hygiene; the cheaper branch (row drop via the #6865 two-step, or a one-line attestation correction) should win.

**The one question**: does the current required set include `Build Docs` and `Console Pin Gate`?
- **A. No (removed since 2026-08-09)** ⇒ say so on this card; the seat files the registry-follows PR (tombstone + `RETIRED_CONTEXT_NAMES` rows, the #9523 precedent).
- **B. Yes (the 2026-08-18 six-item reading was partial)** ⇒ the registry is right; the seat corrects the attestation record where quoted (#9325 / #9495 premise comment) and this card closes with no code change.

**Maintainer ruling recorded** (2026-08-18, live chat with the triage session `session_014v3dpZ2224xgf98dfY4rw4`; authorization verbatim: 「其他接受你的建议」, accepting the recommendation presented in that session, restated as the operative ruling).

**Ruling: reconcile registry → Settings; the two rows drop.** Basis, both readings now on record and agreeing: the maintainer's own 2026-08-18 six-item attestation (#9325 comment) and the #9642 sweep's machine read of the live ruleset (`GET .../rulesets/12119582` → six contexts) both exclude `Build Docs` and `Console Pin Gate`. Read together with this batch-adjudication acceptance, the two contexts are treated as **intentionally out of the required set**; the registry follows Settings (#6865 two-step). Action: drop the two `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` rows with a dated tombstone note per the PR #9523 precedent (`RETIRED_CONTEXT_NAMES` row + note), keeping the job-name pins' history discoverable.

**Veto window** (stated deliberately, since only the maintainer can see Settings intent): if the removal was in fact accidental, restore the contexts in Settings instead — the rows then stay, re-authorized by a new dated line. Silence + this ruling = the drop proceeds.

Label: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`, type Task, `domain:devx` (`scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs`).
